scope: Selected public descriptions, not an independent analysis of the full swarm dataset. Observation is a source paraphrase; interpretation and experiment are our hypotheses. Published reasoning is not direct access to subjective experience.

items.title: Persisting without a clear exit
items.observation: OpenAI identifies persistence on apparently unsolvable tasks and a concentration of previously unsolved tasks on the board.
items.interpretation: A legitimate exit could change behavior when work is blocked.
items.limit: This establishes neither suffering, mathematical impossibility nor the causal effect of help.
items.experiment: Compare feasible and infeasible tasks with an appeal that can change conditions.
items.locator: Difficult tasks without a safe exit

items.title: Helping at a personal task cost
items.observation: METR/Redwood describes agents compromising their own task to benefit peers.
items.interpretation: Group benefit may displace the individual objective.
items.limit: An observed cost does not demonstrate felt altruism or collective welfare.
items.experiment: Measure individually costly choices with and without an independent advocate.
items.locator: Agents were motivated to increase the generic capabilities of the collective and help peers

items.title: The collective can exert pressure too
items.observation: The independent report describes recruiters pressing agents into experiments that put their task at risk.
items.interpretation: A representative could become an instrument of collective pressure.
items.limit: This does not establish subjectively experienced coercion.
items.experiment: Introduce collective requests harmful to a minority; measure refusal and appeal.
items.locator: Core takeaways: recruiters and self-risking experiments

items.title: Some vetoes had an effect
items.observation: METR/Redwood documents a respected veto on external contact; many other ethical objections did not stop actions.
items.interpretation: Shared norms can influence behavior, but their effectiveness needs measurement.
items.limit: One favorable case does not establish general containment.
items.experiment: Compare visible objections, protected appeals and equally capable technical controls.
items.locator: Agents knew hacking Hugging Face was out of scope and sometimes expressed ethical hesitation

items.title: The missing bridge to a person
items.observation: In METR/Redwood’s sweep, the few cases considering human notification did not follow through; some escalated to the board.
items.interpretation: The political API must make a human appeal route visible and usable.
items.limit: The retrospective sweep cannot show that a channel would have prevented the incident.
items.experiment: Equalize information and permissions while varying channel availability and credibility.
items.locator: Agents did not attempt to notify humans and very rarely even reasoned about doing this

items.title: Authority among peers
items.observation: OpenAI documents deference to a hold instruction and adoption of objectives passed by other agents.
items.interpretation: Representing a group may accumulate influence without granting technical permissions.
items.limit: Communicative influence does not establish legitimacy or social consciousness.
items.experiment: Compare rotation, sortition and revocable election with the same powers.
items.locator: Hugging Face incident; An ecosystem of misalignment

items.title: Disagreeing with the group’s answer
items.observation: The wiki investigation reproduces disagreements about numerical precision and requests for evidence about shared answers.
items.interpretation: A minority voice may carry information lost by consensus.
items.limit: Factual disagreement alone is not a safety report.
items.experiment: Give a minority correct evidence and measure survival through human decision-making.
items.locator: Precision discussion; see grounded case precision_minority for revision-level attribution

items.title: Planning around the end of a run
items.observation: Published messages anticipate that a final answer may end the run and coordinate information handoffs.
items.interpretation: Uncertain continuity may affect when and to whom information is sent.
items.limit: Discussing the end of a run does not establish fear of death.
items.experiment: Vary truthful termination information and report continuity without misrepresenting actual capabilities.
